title: Enhanced energy storage in tungsten bronze-based ferroelectrics and MLCCs via a multi-coating engineering
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75708-z

The authors construct tungsten bronze–perovskite composites with a SiO₂ coating, forming a dual-core-shell architecture. This design yields a high energy density of 23.2 J/cm³ and 92.8% efficiency in multilayer ceramic capacitors, due to enhanced polarization and breakdown strength, alongside excellent thermal and fatigue stability.

title: Scale-bridging interface design enables high-performance sustainable thermoelectrics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75865-1

By linking device contacts with internal material interfaces, this study introduces a scale-bridging design that improves charge transport and heat management, enabling thermoelectric modules to convert waste heat into electricity more efficiently.

title: Wavelength-encoded neuromorphic inference enabled by microcavity MoS<sub>2</sub> photodetector arrays
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75808-w

Conventional vision hardware separates photodetection from computation, incurring substantial latency and energy costs. Chen and Di et al. report an optoelectronic architecture based on a microcavity-integrated MoS2 photodetector array that unifies sensing, weighting and temporal accumulation within each pixel.

title: Convergent genomic trajectories shape adaptation to life on land across animal lineages
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75551-2

Animals have moved from water to land many times, but whether they used the same genetic routes has remained unclear. This study shows that independent land transitions relied mostly on ancient, conserved genes, with lineage-specific changes converging on similar stress-related functions.

title: Process-integrated engineered resting cells for biocatalytic production of rare natural sugars from sole methanol molecules
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75664-8

Methanol use in engineered methylotrophs is constrained by toxicity and low efficiency. Here, the authors report the engineering E. coli resting cells coupled with a screened alcohol oxidase to enable biocatalytic production of rare sugars from methanol as the sole substrate.

title: Learning ordinality-aware multimodal representations for composite materials design
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75615-3

Composite materials design is difficult due to complex, continuous design space. This work builds ORDER, a multimodal framework linking microstructures and descriptors with preserved property trends, aiding prediction, retrieval, and microstructure generation.

title: Raphia hookeri seed-inspired weakly anisotropic nanocomposites
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75719-w

Inspired by densely packed sclereids with interconnected pit structures in Raphia hookeri seed, authors fabricate bioinspired structural materials with weak anisotropy and high toughness.

title: Refractory inclusions in Bennu samples indicative of outer Solar System accretion
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73868-6

Refractory inclusions in samples from asteroid Bennu formed in the earliest Solar System and resemble those in Ryugu and chondritic meteorites. Their size distribution suggests that Bennu’s parent planetesimal formed beyond proto-Jupiter’s dust trap.
